To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) African‐American men are diagnosed with penile cancer at younger ages, have a higher rate of locally advanced or metastatic disease, and are less likely to receive treatment; (2) African‐American patients are less likely to be alive 5 years after diagnosis; and (3) African‐American and white men with metastatic penile cancer have similar survival outcomes.
African‐American men with penile squa-mous cell carcinoma have a significantly worse overall survival than Caucasian American men.
